title: Equivariant map
description: Maps whose domain and codomain are acted on by the same group, and the map commutes
extract: In mathematics, equivariance is a form of symmetry for functions from one space with symmetry to another. A function is said to be an equivariant map when its domain and codomain are acted on by the same symmetry group, and when the function commutes with the action of the group. That is, applying a symmetry transformation and then computing the function produces the same result as computing the function and then applying the transformation.
